findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile d458 and a881: state explicitly whether transition replay may consult create_defaults for required transition fields, and if so assign the wiring to a child (currently owned by neither).
evidence: d458 Approach: 'a required field with no create_defaults/known value aborts'
a881 Approach: 'create_defaults: a per-project table ... applied only at issue-create time ... write-only-on-create and not reconciled thereafter'
Parent AC7 scopes create_defaults to 'required-custom-field create failures'
findings.finding: Conflicting assumption between d458 (S6) and a881 (S5)/parent about where create_defaults applies. d458's un-clean-hop criterion aborts a transition hop when it needs 'an un-fillable required field (no create_defaults/known value)', consulting create_defaults during a TRANSITION. But a881 and the parent scope create_defaults as 'applied only at issue-create time... write-only-on-create and not reconciled thereafter'. A transition is not a create, so it is undefined whether create_defaults values are even available to the replay path, and neither child owns the transition-field-fill behavior.
scenarios: A Jira transition screen marks a field required; replay in S6 checks create_defaults for a fill value, but S5 only wired create_defaults into the create payload path, so the lookup finds nothing (or is undefined) and every such hop drifts even when the operator supplied the value under create_defaults.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the 'create_defaults' reference from d458's un-clean-hop criterion (transitions never fill from create_defaults; any required transition field ⇒ drift), or add an explicit criterion/owner for transition-time field fill.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in S6 how the local STATUS-event hop sequence is mapped through the seam to Jira status names and how consecutive hops that collapse to the same Jira state (non-injective forward map) are deduplicated before each single-hop transition_issue_by_name attempt, so redundant/no-op hops do not count against the give-up bound.
evidence: Plan: 'derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log ... anchors on Jira's current status, and re-attempts each intermediate hop through that existing single-hop primitive'

acli.py transition_issue_by_name takes a Jira status name and RAISES RuntimeError when 'no transition reaches <target>' — a redundant no-op hop against an already-current Jira state would surface as such a failure
findings.finding: S6's transition-replay mechanism does not specify how the local hop sequence (drawn from the core STATUS event log, which records LOCAL status values) is translated through the mapping seam into Jira status names, nor how it deduplicates hops that collapse to the same Jira state under the non-injective forward status map.
findings.location: Approach section (S6 replay paragraph) and Child S6
scenarios: A ticket whose local history is open -> in_progress -> blocked -> in_progress: the last two local hops both map to Jira 'In Progress', so a literal per-local-hop replay attempts a Jira transition to a state the issue is already in
Anchoring on Jira's current status when several trailing local hops collapse to that same Jira state — the replay must skip them rather than count them against the give-up bound

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the S6 Approach, justify local-event-log hop replay against the established alternative of querying Jira's available transitions and pathfinding over the workflow transition graph, recording why replay's reachability trade-offs are acceptable (or adopting/hybridizing the graph approach).
evidence: Plan: 'S6 adds new dispatcher logic that derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log ... anchors on Jira's current status, and re-attempts each intermediate hop through that existing single-hop primitive'
Plan flags this as novel: 'S6's replay algorithm itself is new code' and 'the reconciler today has no hop-recording machinery'

External prior art on the same problem centers on the Jira workflow transition graph, not on replaying the source system's own history: Atlassian 'create-workflow-transitions' / 'working-with-workflows' (statuses+transitions graph), SD Elements and ONEiO illegal-transition handling — none of which the plan cites or contrasts

The two approaches differ in reachability: replaying LOCAL recorded hops assumes each local hop name maps to a Jira transition that is available in sequence, whereas a Jira-transition-graph search finds a path that is actually reachable in the target workflow even when it diverges from rebar's local hop history
findings.finding: S6's transition-replay algorithm is genuinely novel code, but the plan adopts local-event-log hop replay without considering the established prior-art alternative (query Jira's available transitions from the current status and pathfind over the workflow transition graph to the target) that mature tracker-sync tools use for the same illegal-transition problem.
findings.location: Approach section (transition replay paragraph) and S6 child; AC line 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay of rebar's recorded hops'
scenarios: A REB ticket whose local hop history was open->in_progress->done but whose Jira workflow only permits open->blocked->done: local-hop replay attempts a non-existent Jira path and drifts, where a workflow-graph search would have found the reachable open->blocked->done path
A target whose current Jira status was reached out-of-band (not via a rebar hop), so anchoring on 'Jira's current status' plus a local hop sequence has no valid continuation
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short prior-art paragraph to S6 contrasting (a) replaying rebar's recorded local hops vs (b) reading Jira's available-transitions endpoint and doing a BFS to the target status over the actual workflow graph; state the chosen algorithm's assumptions (local hop names resolve to available Jira transitions in order) and why the graph-walk alternative was rejected or folded in as the anchor step before give-up->drift.

No sibling roster AC states 'composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants' or 'existing reconciler suite passes unchanged'
findings.finding: Parent AC1 ('A project with no overrides syncs byte-for-identical to today's behavior — verified by the existing reconciler suite passing unchanged AND a test asserting the composed default map equals the current hardcoded constants') is only partially covered: no sibling in the roster owns either verification limb. scenarios: S1/S2 land, each axis resolves through the seam with an identity default, but a subtle merge-precedence or fallback bug shifts a default value; because no child owns the composed-default-equals-hardcoded assertion, the byte-identical regression escapes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit acceptance criterion to bfe7 (S1) or 438a (S2): 'the composed default map (no config) equals the current hardcoded constants (LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA/LOCAL_TYPE_TO_JIRA/LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA/RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK) and the existing reconciler suite passes unchanged'.
